caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 987 of 2011
lawyer:
Muksedur Rahman, Advocate instructed by Chowdhury Md. Zahangir, Advocate-on-Record   For the Petitioner
Khaled Ahmed, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent No.1  
Respondent Nos.2- 12 ------ Not represented
parties:
Alhaj Md. Taher Ali ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Md. Mohiuddin Ahmed and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J.: This Civil Petition for leave to appeal has been directed against the judgment and order dated 27.04.20011 passed by  a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 595 or 2011 discharging the rule and affirming the judgment and decree dated 30.11.2010 passed by the Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 339 of 2009 affirming the judgment and decree dated 16.02.2009 passed by the Senior. Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 41 of 200.6 disposing of the suit on the basis of solenama. 

 7. Mr. Muksedur Rahman, the learned advocate has made submissions to the effect that the plaintiff-respondent No. 1 was dismissed from service on specific allegations and Following the rules and that dismissal order was also approved by the Higher Secondary Education Board, Dhaka and as such the defendant No. 2 of the suit had no authority to compromise the suit with the plaintiff allowing the plaintiff to get a decree in his favour. That all the courts below including the High Court Division have failed to consider that there was collusion in between the plaintiff and the defendant No. 2 and the solenama Filed in the court was collusive one and as such the decree in terms of solenama has been illegal. The learned advocate for the petitioner has argued also that the. High court Division failed to notice also that there was no decision of the governing body to compromise the suit and in the circumstances the solenama filed by the principal of the institution was not acceptable at all. The learned advocate has submitted further that the petitioner, admittedly, is a founder member of the institution in question and, therefore, he is highly concerned about this institution and that the High Court Division without taking into consideration this fact most arbitrarily discharged the rule holding that the petitioner is not at all an interested party. 

 8. Mr. Khaled Ahmed, the learned advocate for respondent No. 1 has submitted that the managing committee or even any member thereof have not come before the court to challenge the genuineness of the solenama and that this present petitioner is none of the managing committee and as such his objection as to the solenama filed in the court and also accepted by the court cannot be entertained at all. That the appellate court below rightly dismissed the appeal preferred by this petitioner challenging we said solenama and the High Court Division also rightly discharged the rule obtained challenging the judgment and decree of the appellate court below. 

 10. It appears that the High Court Division, on examination and consideration of the facts and circumstances on record found out that the trial court being satisfied about genuineness of the solenama accepted the same and consequently decreed the suit in terms of that solenama and that none of Governing Body of the institution ever raised any objection anywhere against that sole decree, that this petitioner though claimed himself to be the founder member of the institution, but he could not show any reason for which the solenama could be treated as illegal and also could not prove that by that sole decree he had been prejudiced in any way.
